topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, her background, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes, carcinogenicity, and tumor promotion.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Bad Luck versus Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what drives cancer by weighing intrinsic cellular errors and bad luck against environmental exposures, supported by global epidemiological and migration data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis by Infectious, Chemical, and Physical Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific pathogens, dietary toxins, radiation, and xenobiotic chemicals interact with host metabolism to cause direct or indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing cooperate with mutagenic initiators to enable neoplastic outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Evaluating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo animal, and in vitro bacterial testing methods used to establish whether an agent causes cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Everyday Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with final framing on balancing daily risks and benefits associated with environmental carcinogens.
